label: 2–8 November
notes: Cook in number order: salmon and prawns first while they're freshest.
Breakfast is overnight oats: make the jars on Sunday, 10 minutes.
Menu approved by you on Thursday (kept all 5). 4 of the 5 dinners use the Air Fryer.
Nutrition is estimated per serving from ingredient weights.

breakfast.title: Berry, chia & almond overnight oats

ingredients.item: Tesco Free From Pure Oats (certified GF)

steps.text: Per 2 jars (one day for both of you): in a bowl, stir 60g oats, 10g chia and ⅛ tsp salt.
Stir in 300g yoghurt and 120ml almond drink until no dry oats are left. It looks loose; the oats and chia thicken it overnight.
Split between 2 jars or boxes. Top each with 80g frozen berries straight from the freezer (they thaw overnight and bleed into the oats). Lid on, fridge for at least 6 hours, up to 3 days.
In the morning, stir, then scatter 10g chopped almonds on each. Eat cold.
Taste: if it's too sharp, stir in 1 tsp honey (+20 kcal). Too thick? Stir in 1 tbsp (15ml) almond drink.

breakfast.tip: Make 3 days' worth (6 jars) on Sunday and 2 days' worth (4 jars) when they run out. Add the almonds in the morning so they stay crunchy.

dinners.title: Air Fryer salmon, crispy potatoes & green beans with lemon-dill yoghurt

ingredients.item: olive oil (2 tsp potatoes, 1 tsp salmon)
salt (½ potatoes, ½ bean water, ⅛ salmon, ⅛ yoghurt, ⅛ finish)

steps.text: Potatoes: toss the halved potatoes with 2 tsp oil, ½ tsp salt and ⅛ tsp pepper.
Air Fryer: potatoes at 200°C for 20 min, shaking at 10 min. Done when golden and a knife slides in easily. Tip them into a bowl and cover with a plate.
Salmon: pat the fillets dry with kitchen roll. Rub with 1 tsp oil, the zest of ½ lemon, ⅛ tsp salt and ⅛ tsp pepper.
Air Fryer: salmon at 200°C for 8–10 min. Done when it flakes easily and is opaque in the middle (60°C). For the last 2 min, put the potatoes back in around it to re-crisp.
Meanwhile, beans: boil 1 litre water with ½ tsp salt. Add the beans for 3–4 min, until tender but still bright green. Drain.
Dill yoghurt: chop 15g dill. Stir it into 150g yoghurt with the grated ½ garlic clove, the rest of the lemon zest, 2 tbsp lemon juice and ⅛ tsp salt.
Taste the yoghurt: if flat, add ⅛ tsp salt; too sharp, 1 tbsp more yoghurt. Serve the salmon on the potatoes and beans with a big spoon of the sauce, the last 5g dill chopped over and lemon wedges.

dinners.tip: The potatoes need their own ½ tsp salt: the sauce only seasons what it touches. Keep the other 600g of potatoes for the weekend.

dinners.title: Prawn pad Thai with rice noodles, egg & beansprouts

ingredients.item: spring onions (whites and greens sliced separately)

steps.text: Noodles: put 100g vermicelli in a bowl with ½ tsp salt and pour over 1 litre boiling water. Soak 4 min (check the pack), then drain, rinse under the cold tap and shake dry.
Sauce: mix 2 tbsp tamari, 2 tsp fish sauce, 2 tsp honey, 2 tbsp lime juice, ¼ tsp chilli flakes and 30ml water.
Heat 1 tsp oil in a wok on high. Beat the 2 eggs, pour in and scramble for 1 min until just set. Tip onto a plate. (No salt: the sauce seasons them.)
Add 2 tsp oil, the pepper strips, the spring onion whites and the garlic. Stir-fry 2 min.
Add the prawns (patted dry) and stir-fry 2–3 min, until pink all through and curled into a C.
Add the noodles and the sauce. Toss with tongs for 1–2 min, until the sauce is absorbed. Add the beansprouts and egg and toss 1 min more; the sprouts should stay crunchy.
Taste: tamari and fish sauce season it, so no salt. If flat, add 1 tsp tamari; too salty, a squeeze of lime. Serve with the almonds, spring onion greens, coriander and lime wedges.

dinners.tip: Have everything chopped before the wok goes on: it cooks in under 8 minutes. Real pad Thai uses tamarind; lime does the same job here.

dinners.title: Beef kofta with herby quinoa, cucumber-tomato salad & garlic yoghurt

ingredients.item: red onion (½ grated for the kofta, ¼ thinly sliced)
flat leaf parsley, chopped (10g kofta, 5g quinoa)
olive oil (1 tsp kofta, 2 tsp salad)
salt (½ kofta, ¼ quinoa, ⅛ salad, ⅛ yoghurt)

steps.text: Quinoa: rinse 80g quinoa in a sieve for 30 sec. Pan with 200ml water and ¼ tsp salt. Boil, then lid on, lowest heat, 12 min. Off the heat, lid on, 5 min, then fluff and stir in 5g parsley.

Kofta: in a bowl, mix the mince with the grated ½ onion, 1 grated garlic clove, 10g parsley, 1 tsp cumin, ½ tsp smoked paprika, ½ tsp oregano, ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper. Squeeze it together with your hand for 1 min so it holds.
Shape into 6 sausages about 10cm long. Brush with 1 tsp oil.
Air Fryer: kofta at 200°C for 10–12 min, turning at 6 min. Done when browned and 71°C in the middle, with no pink.
Salad: toss the cucumber, tomatoes and the sliced ¼ onion with 1 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tsp oil and ⅛ tsp salt.
Garlic yoghurt: stir 80g yoghurt with ½ grated garlic clove, 1 tsp lemon juice and ⅛ tsp salt.
Taste the kofta: if flat, a pinch more salt goes on the salad (⅛ tsp); if rich, more lemon. Serve quinoa, salad, 3 kofta each and the yoghurt.

dinners.tip: Take the 150g freezer bag out the day before. The rest of the fresh pack (390g) gets frozen on Sunday in 2 bags.

dinners.title: Chicken fajita rice bowls with black beans, peppers & lime

ingredients.item: salt (½ chicken & veg, ¼ rice, ⅛ beans)

steps.text: Rice: rinse 80g rice for 30 sec. Pan with 140ml water and ¼ tsp salt. Boil, then lid on, lowest heat, 10 min. Off the heat, lid on, 5 min.
Chicken: in a bowl mix 1 tbsp oil, the garlic, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp cumin, ½ tsp oregano, ¼ tsp chilli flakes, ½ tsp salt and ⅛ tsp pepper. Add the chicken, peppers and onion and toss to coat.
Air Fryer: 200°C for 14–16 min, shaking at 5 and 10 min. Chicken done at 75°C or when the juices run clear; the peppers should be charred at the edges.
Beans: drain and rinse the tin. Warm 100g in a small pan with ¼ tsp cumin, ⅛ tsp salt and 1 tbsp water for 3 min. Off the heat, add 1 tbsp lime juice. Freeze the rest of the beans.
Squeeze 1 tbsp lime juice over the chicken and veg.
Taste a piece of chicken: if flat, ⅛ tsp salt over the pan; too hot, more yoghurt. Serve: rice, beans, chicken and peppers, 30g yoghurt each, coriander, spring onions and lime wedges.

dinners.tip: The spice rub is all-homemade, so it's gluten-free with no label to check. Freeze the other 300g of chicken on Sunday.

dinners.title: Halloumi, roast aubergine & lentil salad with lemon-oregano dressing

ingredients.item: salt (¼ veg, ⅜ lentils, ⅛ dressing)

steps.text: Lentils: rinse 70g lentils. Simmer in 750ml water for 20–25 min, until tender but holding their shape. Add ⅜ tsp salt for the last 5 min. Drain well.
Veg: toss the aubergine and onion with 2 tsp oil, ½ tsp oregano, ¼ tsp salt and ⅛ tsp pepper.
Air Fryer: veg at 200°C for 12 min, shaking at 6 min. Then lay the halloumi slices on top and cook 6–8 min more, until golden at the edges. (No salt on the halloumi: it's salty already.)
Dressing: whisk 2 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tsp oil, the grated ½ garlic clove, ½ tsp oregano, ⅛ tsp salt and ⅛ tsp pepper.
Toss the warm lentils with the spinach (it wilts a little), tomatoes, parsley and most of the dressing.
Taste the lentils: if flat, ⅛ tsp salt or 1 tsp lemon; the halloumi will add salt, so keep them a touch under. Top with the veg and halloumi and spoon over the last of the dressing.

dinners.tip: Tesco had no light halloumi, so this uses regular: the portion is 100g each to stay under 600 kcal.

tips: Chicken: put 300g in the fridge for 4. Freeze the other 300g flat in a labelled bag.
Mince: weigh out 110g for 3 into a box in the fridge. Freeze the other 390g in 2 labelled bags of 195g.
Make 6 breakfast jars (3 days' worth). See the breakfast recipe.
Wrap the dill, coriander and parsley in damp kitchen roll in a box.
Cook the extra 600g potatoes too if you want them for the weekend: same Air Fryer time, fridge within 1 hour.
Move the 150g bag of mince from the freezer to the fridge.
Optional: cook 4's rice too (80g rice, 140ml water, ¼ tsp salt). Fridge it within 1 hour; reheat once only, until piping hot.

prep.when: When the breakfast jars run out
tips: Make 4 more jars (2 days' worth): 120g oats, 20g chia, ¼ tsp salt, 600g yoghurt, 240ml almond drink, 320g berries.
Black beans: about 140g left from 4. Freeze them for a future chilli.
Spinach: about 130g left after 5. Wilt it into weekend eggs.
Cucumber: half is left after 3, and 100g beansprouts after 2: snacks with the sugarsnaps.
Limes: 1½ in 2, 1½ in 4, 2 spare. Lemons: 1 each in 1, 3 and 5, 1 spare.
Yoghurt: 2kg bought. Breakfasts use 1.5kg; 1, 3 and 4 use 290g.
Almonds: 100g for breakfasts, 20g in 2, the rest (plus last week's 80g) are snacks.

skipped: Salt & vinegar rice cakes (you said no rice crackers this week)
Chicken from the freezer (you'd finished it), so fresh thighs instead
